name: por-output-chain-deglitch
description: Deglitch dwell, qualifying-brownout-dip capture and chatter rejection of design/por_output_chain.sch, at nominal and (since issue #221) the real worst-case delivered IBIAS, over the full 81-point PVT grid. Post-layout composite netlist. The stress DUT (xdut2) was re-cut by #221 from an idealised 0.5x nominal (0.25 uA) to 91.0251 nA -- 0.182x nominal, the worst-case current sim/por-output-chain-ibias-sharing/'s post-layout record measures the assembly actually delivering to this cell's own IBIAS pin across both RESETn states. This turns the stress DUT's brownout check (dwell_pgdg_halfib_us, now restated as the voltage floor pgdg_min_during_halfib_dip_v) from a PASS into a FAIL at the cold corners -- see spec/decision-records/DR-024-por-output-chain-real-ibias-delivery.md. Since #200 the grid also carries the filter's glitch-rejection WIDTH margin: a third chatter burst at 1.05 us (5 % wider than the 1 us the checks above use), with the one-shot's own charge loss recorded as tim_loss_wide_pct and tim_loss_1us_pct. Those two are deliberately limit-free -- they are the margin, and a bound on them would only ever report a flip, not the movement that precedes it. The width matters most against this netlist: control/width_results.md brackets its rejection ceiling between 1.0 and 1.25 us at the fastest corners, against 1.75-2.0 us for the schematic.
claim: spec/target-spec.md#por-brownout -- fills that row's open TBD by publishing the deglitch dwell time this cell designs to, and shows it stays under the row's T_dip,min = 10 us so a qualifying dip re-asserts RESETn and regenerates the full spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-pulse. Also covers the no-early/no-double-pulse edge case: sub-dwell POR_RAW chatter, applied both during assertion and after release, changes nothing at the pin. Deglitch is this cell's time-domain mechanism per DR-005 and is separate from the comparator's static hysteresis (#10). Deterministic corners only -- the full brownout sweep is #14's job. Post-layout re-run (#86) against layout/postlayout/por_output_chain.spice (#82/PR #180, direct klt extraction): XCDG/XCTIM are real drawn-and-extracted MiM caps plus the drawn interconnect's own parasitic R/C on the signal path -- not a schematic-ideal cap with added parasitics, since every device in this cell is drawn (0 ideal, layout/postlayout/AUDIT.md). See design/por_output_chain.md's post-layout section for the schematic-vs-extracted pulse-width/dwell delta.

pgdg_min_during_halfib_dip_v.description: THE por-brownout check, restated as a threshold rather than a crossing TIME: a qualifying 10 us POR_RAW dip must pull the filter output (PGDG) below its 1.0 V trip point -- i.e. the dwell must not exceed T_dip,min = 10 us -- measured on the stress DUT over the qualifying dip ITSELF (12.000-12.010 ms), so 'below 1.0 V somewhere in this window' is exactly 'dwell <= 10 us' with no slack borrowed from after POR_RAW returns high. Since #221 the stress DUT's IBIAS is 91.0251 nA (0.182x nominal) -- the real worst-case current sim/por-output-chain-ibias-sharing/'s post-layout record measures the assembly delivering to this pin, not an idealised 0.5x. At this current the filter is often too slow to trip AT ALL within the 10 us dip (PGDG droops and then recovers as POR_RAW returns high), which is why this check is a voltage floor rather than 'dwell_pgdg_halfib_us' (a WHEN-based crossing-time measure, kept for the DR-005-nominal DUT above): a crossing-time measure errors out of its search interval on exactly the corners this record needs to show FAILING, rather than reporting a FAIL. A value at or above 1.0 V means the qualifying dip was rejected outright, not merely late. EXPECTED TO FAIL (i.e. NOT drop below 1.0 V) at the cold corners until a lever from DR-024 lands. Binds at ss/-40c/res_ss/-40c

dwell_pgdg_1x_us.description: same dwell at the DR-005 nominal 0.5 uA IBIAS -- the number published against the spec row's TBD

reassert_validlow_us.description: end-to-end: POR_RAW falling to RESETn at a valid logic low (0.3 V) at the pin, including the release NAND and the output driver. This is what a downstream digital domain actually sees

resetn_min_during_dip.description: the qualifying 10 us dip really does re-assert RESETn to a valid low -- not a partial droop. A dwell that crept over 10 us at some corner fails here even if the crossing measurement above found something

resetn_max_after_dip.description: no double pulse: after the dip the FULL pulse regenerates, so RESETn stays asserted to the end of the run (the shortest pulse anywhere on the grid is >4 ms; this window is 0.5 ms)

pgdg_min_during_chatter.description: three 1 us sub-dwell glitches on POR_RAW do not move the filter output at all -- this is the deglitch doing its job, measured where it happens

resetn_max_during_chatter.description: no early release: chatter while the pulse is still running never lets RESETn go high

pgdg_min_during_wide_chatter.description: #200's width-margin check. Three 1.05 us glitches -- 5 % wider than the 1 us burst above -- applied after the qualifying dip has restarted the pulse, still leave the filter output near the rail. 1.05 us is inside the bracket control/width_results.md measures the rejection ceiling in at the two fastest corners (post-layout: rejected at 1.0 us, disturbed at 1.25 us; schematic: 1.75 / 2.0 us), so it is a wider width the design AS DRAWN still passes at every corner rather than a width picked for comfort. The 2.0 V bound sits below the worst point this manifest produces -- 2.45 V post-layout at ff/125 C/2.97 V, 2.93 V schematic -- and well above the 1.27 V a glitch that actually propagates leaves behind (width_results.md, post-layout ff/125 C/3.63 V at 1.25 us)

tim_min_during_wide_chatter_v.description: the functional half of #200's width-margin check, and the half with the teeth: across the wider burst the one-shot's timer node keeps its charge. A glitch that propagates fires XMDIS and slams TIM to within tens of mV of VSS -- the CDG = 98 fF failure design/por_output_chain.md records -- and that, not PGDG drooping, is the functional failure (it is also the quantity control/width_results.md's rejected/partial/through verdict is defined on). Undisturbed, TIM sits at 0.39-0.58 V here across the grid, so 0.25 V separates 'kept its charge' from 'restarted' with margin at every corner. It is deliberately NOT a bound on the margin itself: the margin is tim_loss_wide_pct, which carries no limit so that a re-run reports it moving rather than only flipping

resetn_min_after_release.description: no spurious re-assertion: the same chatter applied after release never pulls RESETn down

tpulse_after_chatter_ms.description: the pulse is neither truncated nor restarted by the chatter. The upper bound is the discriminator: a glitch that got through would have reset the timer at 1.2 ms and pushed the release ~0.9 ms later than the un-chattered pulse recorded in sim/por-output-chain-pulse/

iq_asserted_1x_na.description: reset-asserted draw before POR_RAW goes high; third independent measurement of this cell's por-iq share

netlist_provenance_note: por_output_chain: 33 drawn devices, 0 ideal -- every device including the deglitch one-shot's XCDG/XCTIM MiM caps (5 total) is drawn and extracted, not schematic-ideal. 18/30 nets carry parasitic R/C (ΣR 66322 Ω, ΣC 828.6 fF). 12 body/plate/well ties (NW1->VDD, XCDG/XCTIM plate+VSS ties, vsubs->VSS) applied per the schematic since the extraction deck's connectivity stack does not reach them. The 5 MiM caps are extracted as cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield and emitted as the electrically-identical cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield (klayout-tools#315, same 2.0 fF/um^2 device, stack-variant name only). Per layout/postlayout/AUDIT.md.
